title: Give Thanks
subtitle: The Life That Says Thank You
tagline: What we do with what we’ve received is the loudest thank-you we’ll ever say.
headline: The Life That Says Thank You
headline_sub: When Gratitude Becomes a Way of Living
seo_title: The Life That Says Thank You: Colossians 3:17
seo_description: Whatever you do, give thanks. A Thanksgiving Eve devotional for men on gratitude as a way of living, and telling what God has done at your Thanksgiving table.
og_image_alt: The Life That Says Thank You: What we do with what we’ve received is the loudest thank-you we’ll ever say. TheWrkShop.

scriptures.text: Let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts, since as members of one body you were called to peace. And be thankful.
And whatever you do, whether in word or deed, do it all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through him.

blocks.text: Paul does something remarkable.
He doesn’t isolate thanksgiving as a single activity.
He connects it with:
And finally:
Whatever you do. Give thanks.
GRATITUDE IS NOT MERELY SOMETHING WE EXPRESS. IT CAN BECOME HOW WE LIVE.
That changes Thanksgiving.
Instead of one day when we count blessings, gratitude becomes a posture that shapes everyday decisions.

items: How we steward what we’ve received.

blocks.text: “GRATITUDE IS SOMETHING I FEEL WHEN LIFE IS GOING WELL.”
Feelings matter.
But feelings fluctuate.
Some mornings we wake up encouraged.
Other mornings we wake up burdened.
If gratitude depends entirely on how we feel, it will disappear whenever life gets hard.
Paul points to something deeper.
A life increasingly shaped by Christ.
But a growing recognition that everything we do belongs under His lordship.
Consider this movement:
Now imagine gratitude entering that process.

items: We become more attentive to grace.
We notice gifts we used to overlook.

blocks.text: GRATITUDE TURNS OUR EYES TOWARD GOD’S GOODNESS. AND WHAT WE BEHOLD, WE BECOME.
As we behold Christ, the Spirit keeps doing His transforming work (2 Corinthians 3:18).
THE GOAL IS NOT SIMPLY TO BECOME MORE GRATEFUL PEOPLE. IT IS TO BECOME PEOPLE WHO LIVE MORE FAITHFULLY BEFORE CHRIST.
Colossians 3 places thanksgiving inside a bigger picture of the Christian life.
Gratitude is not the center.
Christ is.
Thanksgiving is one expression of a life increasingly aligned with Him.

items: What has God entrusted to me?
Where have I let entitlement grow?
What blessing can I pass forward?
Who needs to hear my appreciation?
What would change if gratitude shaped my leadership, relationships, and decisions?
Does my life merely contain moments of thanksgiving, or is it becoming an expression of thanksgiving?

blocks.text: Before tomorrow’s celebration, take time to remember.

items: And offer your life to Christ again.

blocks.text: Not because gratitude earns His love.
Because His grace invites a faithful response.
Then tomorrow at the table, tell one story of what God did for you this year.
Your kids are listening. That’s Psalm 78 at your Thanksgiving table.
What we do with what we’ve received is the loudest thank-you we’ll ever say.

Father, thank You for Your faithfulness. Thank You for the people, opportunities, provision, and grace You have given me. Forgive my entitlement and inattention. Teach me to receive with humility, remember with gratitude, give with generosity, and live in obedience to Christ. May my life increasingly say thank You. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
What we do with what we’ve received is the loudest thank-you we’ll ever say.
Gratitude can become a way of living, not merely a moment of expression.
Attention to grace can weaken the grip of entitlement.
Gratitude is not the center. Christ is.
—TheWrkShop
